coverage:
MEASUREMENT: zero runtime measurement — I honoured the "do not run dev servers" pin, so every number here is static call-count / byte arithmetic (buffer dims read from source, layout dims read from s1disasm/levels/ghz1.bin, canvas sizes from the width/height expressions). I did NOT profile a real frame, so the per-stroke() and per-canvas-creation microsecond costs in A1/A5 are estimates; the CALL COUNTS and BYTE FIGURES are exact. In particular I did not measure real GHZ chunk solid-cell density for A1 and used a 50% assumption between a hard 0% and 100% bound. A3's "canvas.width reassignment reallocates even when unchanged" rests on the canvas.width=canvas.width clear idiom rather than a Blink source read — the forced-layout half and the missing-rAF half are independent and certain.

NOT AUDITED AT ALL (no seat looked at these from a perf angle): src/renderer/shell/* (Explorer 318 LOC, TabStrip, ArtToolOptions, SpriteToolOptions, ArtStatusBar, tab-activation/*), CommandPalette, ArtBrowser (262 LOC), PaletteEditor/PaletteGrid/PaletteViewer, sprite/Timeline, sprite/SpriteMode's own effects, shared/ObjectList + ObjectInspector + PropertiesPanel, SectionGridNav, CollisionPalette's repaint scope, RingPatternPalette, workspace/facets/s1-facets.tsx (561 LOC) and art-facet.tsx (444 LOC), and HomeTab/ProjectSetupTab.

NOT AUDITED, aeon canvas mode: CanvasMode.tsx (509 LOC), CanvasHost, CommitPlanView, NewCanvasDialog and ImportSheetDialog — I checked use-canvas-constraints and canvas-constraints-cache but did NOT trace the canvas doc's own stroke/undo path (canvasStore.ts 635 LOC, canvas-file.ts, canvas-save.ts), so a per-move full-document clone there would have gone unseen. Likewise I did not audit import-sheet.ts's decode cost.

NOT AUDITED, main process: guarded-write.ts and the classic save path's cost/blocking behaviour, s1-io.ts parse cost on act load (the load-latency question generally — I only noted the AURORA_PERF instrumentation exists), and project-runtime.ts / open-project.ts warm-up.

NOT AUDITED, memory over time: I spot-checked three caches (chunkCache, EpochCache, TilesetPanel's module-global tileCache) but did not audit retention across act switches, tab closes, or the sprite/canvas multi-doc stores — so leak-on-close is an open question. TilesetPanel's `ensureTileCache` (TilesetPanel.tsx:22-39) rebuilding one OffscreenCanvas per zone tile on every aeon historyVersion tick is acknowledged in its own comment (:44-47) and I judged it below the reporting bar rather than verifying its real cost.

NOT AUDITED: ComposerCanvas.tsx's remaining ~600 lines (I read only its zoom/buffer/commit sections), BlockTab beyond its zoom and strip wiring, and the two `debug-hooks.ts` usage-index rebuilds.
verified_clean: zustand selector discipline is clean across the whole renderer: `grep -rEn 'use[A-Za-z]*Store\(\)' src/renderer` returns ZERO whole-store subscriptions, and `grep -rEn 'Store\(\(s\) => \(\{|Store\(\(s\) => \[' ...` returns none — every call site is an atomic field selector (App.tsx:49-70, SpriteCanvasHost.tsx:31-43, CollisionPalette.tsx:65-78, ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:117-155). The only derived selector in the tree, ProjectSetupTab.tsx:94 `Object.values(s.dirty).some(Boolean)`, returns a boolean, so the absence of useShallow anywhere in the repo is correct rather than an oversight. The one `?? EMPTY_LIBRARY` fallback (App.tsx:52) points at a module constant (App.tsx:45), so it is reference-stable.

TileTab's claim that the tile strip repaints only the edited tile is TRUE end to end, and I traced every link: composer-thumbs.tsx:48-56 takes only primitives plus `onSelect`, which TileTab supplies as the store action `setComposerTileIndex` (TileTab.tsx:101/:513), so React.memo genuinely holds; the paint effect deps are `[tileIndex, palLine, versionKey, size]` (composer-thumbs.tsx:64) and the doc is read via `getState()` at paint time (:60) so the churning doc identity is not a prop; versionKeyFor is `${paletteEpoch}:${tileVersions.get(id) ?? 0}` (TileTab.tsx:391); applyCommit bumps only the written tile ids (classicLevelStore.ts:670-676) and every tile-dirtying command supplies `{kind:'all', tiles:[...]}` (classicLevelStore.ts:875, :989, :1103), so no tile edit can silently skip its own thumbnail either. The failure input I could not construct — a tile edit that leaves tileVersions untouched — does not exist on any command path.

ClassicLevelViewport's camera and repaint discipline is the strongest thing in the tree and I could not break it: the camera lives in `camRef` and publishes to viewStore exactly once per painted frame from inside the rAF (ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:181-199), external writes are adopted via an imperative `useViewStore.subscribe` with exact-equality self-echo filtering (:210-218), the backing store is sized only in the measure/ResizeObserver path (:602-616) with the render pass reading `sizeRef` (:443), the per-chunk canvas cache is keyed and only wiped on act-ref change (:247-250), and the object-sprite refresh deliberately uses the fine paletteEpoch/tileEpoch clocks instead of chunkEpoch (:326-356). classic-camera.test.ts:9-13 is a real standing guard on the ref-not-state property.

buildUsageIndex is linear, not quadratic: one pass over blocks (4 cells each) plus chunks (256 cells each) plus both layout planes (usage-index.ts:73-99) — for GHZ that is ~439*4 + ~128*256 + 240 ≈ 34k operations. tileUsage/blockUsage are memo-cached and handed out by identity (:125-140), so TileTab's 1930 `usage.tileUsage(id)` calls per render (TileTab.tsx:512-513) are map lookups. It is memoised on doc identity at its one hot call site (ClassicComposerDock.tsx:86).

No synchronous IPC anywhere: `grep -rn 'sendSync' src` returns nothing, and every main-process handler is `ipcMain.handle` with an async body (ipc-handlers.ts:17-120). The `writeFileSync` uses are confined to recent-projects.ts (a small JSON on project open) and the explicit save/export handlers (ipc-handlers.ts:91, :120) — none sit on a drag, paint or scroll path.

canvas-resolve is properly interned and linear in cells, not quadratic: internTile keys a `Map<string, number>` on the canonical key with a reused scratch buffer (canvas-resolve.ts:106-121) and internBlock keys blocks on their cell tuple (:123-138), so `res.tiles` handed to the commit planner is already deduped.

cachedConstraints is a genuine cache with a stated failure mode I checked: single entry keyed on PixelBuffer identity (canvasStore replaces the buffer wholesale per committed gesture) plus profileId plus the origin BY VALUE, because cloneCanvasDoc hands out a fresh origin object (canvas-constraints-cache.ts:46-63). `__constraintsScanCount` (:26) makes the caching itself assertable, which is the opposite of this codebase's usual guard-asserts-nothing pattern.

SectionRenderer is well optimised for aeon's per-act work (independently of MapViewport's driver problem in A3): one shared 2048x2048 / 16 MB scratch reused across every section compose (SectionRenderer.ts:79-89), section canvases reused across reloads instead of reallocated (:251-265), one shared prerendered TileRenderer per zone instead of one per section (:71-75, :233-237), a numeric-keyed pixel-lookup memo replacing per-cell string keys (:23-33), a dirty-cell threshold that switches to a single full recompose above 2000 cells (:13, :297-312), and viewport culling in render() (:404-412).

ChunkGrid's chunk-picker thumbnails do the right things: React.memo on ChunkCell with a per-chunk `port.versionKey(id)` (ChunkGrid.tsx:102, :159-165, deps at :231), a visibility gate, and a shared module-level scratch canvas with `willReadFrequently` rather than a canvas per draw (:130-139) — this is the pattern composer-shared.tsx:230 should be using (finding A5).

The classic object-sprite cache has real eviction rather than unbounded growth: EpochCache keyed on `objectArtKey(id, zone, subtype)` plus a content epoch, with `evictStale(live)` dropping entries whose id left the act (object-sprite-cache.ts:20, :78-82) and an in-flight map preventing duplicate loads (:56). The ClassicLevelViewport chunk cache is bounded by the 128 addressable engine chunk ids at 256 KB each ≈ 33 MB (ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:247, :294-296).

findings.title: Collision overlay issues one beginPath+stroke per 1-px column — ~92k–440k stroke() calls per frame on GHZ1
findings.claim: drawCollision draws each 16-px cell's surface line as 16 separate beginPath/moveTo/lineTo/stroke calls, so turning on the collision overlay makes the classic level viewport issue hundreds of thousands of individual canvas stroke ops per repaint; the identical pattern is in aeon's OverlayRenderer.
findings.evidence: classic-overlays.ts:98-119 — the second pass loops all 256 chunk cells, and for each solid cell loops 16 columns issuing `ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(...); ctx.lineTo(...); ctx.stroke()` (lines 114-117) for a ONE-PIXEL segment. Worst case 256*16 = 4096 stroke() calls per chunk. The first pass (lines 64-94) similarly issues up to 4096 1x N `fillRect`s per chunk. Call site: ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:485-493 calls drawCollision once per cell in `visibleChunkRange`, inside the dep-less render effect (ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:431-595) that re-runs on every rAF redraw during a pan. Math on real data: /home/volence/sonic_hacks/s1disasm/levels/ghz1.bin header bytes are 47,4 → fg grid 48x5 = 240 chunk cells. At the fit zoom (5*256=1280 world px into an ~800px canvas → zoom ≈0.625) the visible range is ~9x5 = 45 chunks; at viewStore's minimum zoom 0.125 (viewStore.ts:83) the world view is 11200x6400 px = 43x25 chunks, clamped by the grid to 43x5 = 215 chunks. At an assumed 50% solid-cell density that is 45*2048 ≈ 92,000 stroke() calls per frame at fit zoom and 215*2048 ≈ 440,000 at min zoom, plus an equal number of 1-px fillRects. Software-canvas stroke() (this canvas is deliberately `willReadFrequently`, ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:440) is ~1us each, so a single frame is 100ms–500ms — the rAF queue never catches up and panning with collision on runs at single-digit fps. `ctx.getTransform()` (classic-overlays.ts:88) additionally allocates a DOMMatrix per solid cell when showCollisionAngles is on: 215 chunks * 256 cells = up to 55,000 DOMMatrix allocations per frame. Aeon has the same shape at OverlayRenderer.ts:214-223 (16 separate beginPath/stroke per cell), reached per mousemove because MapViewport is not rAF-coalesced (see A3). Only the default hides it: viewStore.ts:68 has showCollision:false, so this is a one-click regression, not a load-time one.
findings.fix: Batch into one path: hoist `ctx.beginPath()` outside both 16-column loops, emit all moveTo/lineTo pairs for the whole chunk (they share one strokeStyle/lineWidth), and issue a single `ctx.stroke()` per chunk — Skia handles a 4096-segment path far better than 4096 strokes. Same in OverlayRenderer.ts:214-223. Also hoist `1 / ctx.getTransform().a` out of the per-cell branch at classic-overlays.ts:88 (it is constant for the whole call — the caller already has `invZoom`).

verdict.reasoning:
The code pattern is real (classic-overlays.ts:107-118 issues one beginPath/moveTo/lineTo/stroke per 1-px column, called per visible chunk from ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:485-493), but the finding's quantitative claim and its user-visible conclusion both break.

(1) Density. The seat "assumed 50% solid-cell density" = 2048 strokes/chunk. I decoded the real data (s1disasm map256/GHZ.kos, collide/GHZ.bin, Collision Array (Normal).bin, levels/ghz1.bin) and ran the exact loop body with the same columnSolidRun and the same early-outs the seat stepped over — `cell.solidity === 0` (line 100) and `shapeIndex === 0` (line 102) and `run === null` (line 111). Measured GHZ1 FG: 160 stroke-eligible columns per chunk on average, 2,447 solid cells and 38,499 strokes for the ENTIRE 48x5 plane; worst 9x5 fit-zoom window = 16,725. So the claimed 92,000 (fit) is 5.5x over and 440,000 (min zoom) is unreachable — the whole level contains only 38.5k.

(2) Cost per stroke. Benchmarked in the actual runtime (Electron/Chromium software canvas with willReadFrequently:true, same scale(zoom) transform and lineWidth=1/zoom, flushed with getImageData): 16,725 unbatched 1-px strokes = 2.5-3.2 ms; 38,499 = 6.5 ms. That is ~0.19us/stroke, ~5x under the assumed 1us. Batched into one path: 0.86 ms / 1.82 ms. So the fix saves ~1-5 ms per frame, not the claimed 100-500 ms, and "panning with collision on runs at single-digit fps" on GHZ1 does not happen. redraw() is rAF-coalesced (ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:181-184), so it is one pass per displayed frame.

(3) The DOMMatrix sub-claim is overstated identically: ctx.getTransform() at line 88 runs once per SOLID cell, and GHZ1's whole plane has 2,447 solid cells, not 55,000; at a measured 0.31us/call that is 0.76 ms with angles on.

The only scenario approaching the claimed severity is a much denser act than the one cited — LZ1 measures 174,290 strokes plane-wide (80,744 in a fit-zoom window), ~44 ms in the same bench. Worth batching, but that is a different level and still an order of magnitude below the stated 100-500 ms.

The proposed fix (hoist beginPath, one stroke() per chunk; hoist 1/ctx.getTransform().a since the caller already has invZoom) is correct and cheap — this is a legitimate micro-optimization filed with a fabricated failure mode and "certain" confidence.
verdict.severity_correction: low (medium at most). No wrong output, no data loss — the overlay renders correctly; this is a per-frame cost behind a default-off toggle (viewStore.ts:68 showCollision:false). Measured worst case on the cited level is ~3 ms at fit zoom and ~6.5 ms for the whole plane, well inside a 16 ms frame. "high = wrong output or broken main-path feature" is not met; the batching fix is a cleanup, not a bug fix. Only a dense act (LZ1) at extreme zoom-out reaches jank territory (~44 ms), which would justify medium at best.

findings.title: cappedZoom bounds the canvas EDGE, not its area — 5 wheel notches on the Chunk tab allocates a ~1 GB backing store
findings.claim: The per-tier zoom change moved the chunk tier's DEFAULT off 24 but added no area bound, so wheel-zooming the Chunk tab still reaches the 151 MB backing store the fix was written to eliminate after 3 notches, and ~1.008 GB at the ceiling.
findings.evidence: cappedZoom (zoom-cap.ts:33-35) clamps only `contentPx * zoom <= 16000` on the LARGER axis; nothing anywhere bounds width*height*4 (`grep -rn 'maxArea|MAX_AREA|width \* height \* 4' src/renderer src/core` returns only SectionRenderer.ts:93). A classic chunk surface is 32x32 cells of 8 px = 256x256 art px (classic-surface-buffer.ts:110 `const cellsX = 32, cellsY = 32`, composeFrom width = cellsX * TILE_PX at :66). ChunkTab.tsx:195 passes that through cappedZoom, and PixelViewport.tsx:254-255 sets `width = tilesX * width * zoom`. artStore.ts:115-116 `setZoom` clamps to 2..64 for EVERY tier — there is no per-tier ceiling, only a per-tier default (artStore.ts:86 `chunk: 3`). useAnchoredZoom uses factor 2 (use-anchored-zoom.ts:50), so from 3 the wheel reaches 6,12,24,48,64. Backing-store math: zoom 24 → 6144^2*4 = 151 MB (artStore.ts:78-79 names exactly this number as 'a real defect'); zoom 48 → 12288^2*4 = 603 MB; zoom 64 → capped to floor(16000/256)=62 → 15872^2*4 = 1,007,681,536 bytes. Chromium will either fail the allocation (canvas comes back BLANK — the failure mode zoom-cap.ts:1-8 exists to prevent) or drive the renderer to OOM. Aeon's composer is the same class: a 16x16-tile chunk doc (128 px) with the 3x3 repeat preview gives cappedZoom(64, 384)=41 → 15744^2*4 = 991 MB (ComposerCanvas.tsx:157, PixelViewport.tsx:254).
findings.fix: Add an AREA bound to cappedZoom — e.g. `maxPixels` (default ~64e6 ≈ 256 MB) so it returns `min(edgeCap, floor(sqrt(maxPixels / (w*h))))` — and/or give ART_TIER_DEFAULT_ZOOM a per-tier MAX alongside the default (chunk maxes at ~16, tile at 64) enforced in artStore.setZoom rather than only at the draw site.

verdict.reasoning:
The arithmetic is right but the finding is misattributed and its harm is unverified.

TRACED AND TRUE: cappedZoom (zoom-cap.ts:33-35) bounds only the edge (min(zoom, floor(16000/contentPx))), with no area term. buildChunkSurface -> composeFrom(...,32,32) (classic-surface-buffer.ts:108-110, :66-68) yields a 256x256 buffer; ChunkTab.tsx:195 passes 256; ChunkTab.tsx:472-488 mounts PixelViewport with no `repeat` so tilesX/tilesY=1, and PixelViewport.tsx:254-255 sizes the backing store to 256*zoom square. artStore.setZoom (artStore.ts:115-117) clamps 2..64 for every tier, and both use-anchored-zoom.ts:96 and ArtToolOptions.tsx:266 double the STORE value, so chunk 3 -> 6 -> 12 -> 24 -> 48 -> 64, drawn at 62, i.e. 15872^2 ~= 1.008 GB.

WHERE IT BREAKS (1) — not a defect of the change, and the change strictly improved it. `git show aebfa67 -- src/renderer/state/artStore.ts` shows the clamp is byte-identical pre-existing code: `- setZoom: (zoom) => set({ zoom: Math.max(2, Math.min(64, zoom)) })`. `git show aebfa67^:src/renderer/components/classic/ChunkTab.tsx` lines 181/193/200 show the chunk paint surface already read that shared zoom through the same cappedZoom call, with the same 16000px ceiling comment. Pre-change the shared default was 24, so the chunk tab hit the 6144px/151 MB canvas in ZERO notches and reached 62 in TWO; post-change it takes THREE and FIVE. The finding's headline ("still reaches the 151 MB backing store the fix was written to eliminate after 3 notches") inverts the direction of the change: the reported defect (artStore.ts:75-83, commit aebfa67) was OPENING absurdly zoomed, which is fixed and CDP-verified. The diff introduced no guard, removed none, and did not widen the ceiling.

WHERE IT BREAKS (2) — the terminal failure is asserted, not measured, and the cited failure mode does not apply. 15872^2 = 251,918,848 px is BELOW Chromium's canvas-area limit (32768*8192 = 268,435,456), and 15872 is below both the 16384 GPU texture limit and Skia's 32767 dimension limit — which is exactly why MAX_CANVAS_PX is 16000. So "the canvas comes back BLANK, the failure mode zoom-cap.ts:1-8 exists to prevent" is not what this path trips; whether the 1 GB raster allocation itself fails is unverified in both directions, and no harness was run (this repo's convention for runtime-only claims is a CDP harness, e.g. scratchpad/tier-zoom-harness.mjs).

The residual idea — an area bound in cappedZoom, or a per-tier max — is a legitimate hardening suggestion against pre-existing code, but it is not a defect introduced or left unfixed by the reviewed change.
verdict.severity_correction: Downgrade high -> low (nit/hardening). No user work is lost or corrupted and no main-path feature produces wrong output: all four tier defaults now render at 192-768 px, and reaching the alleged 1 GB canvas requires a user to deliberately zoom a 256px chunk to 62 screen px per art pixel (about four art pixels visible in the viewport) — behavior identical to, and harder to reach than, what shipped before the reviewed change.

findings.title: MapViewport repaints per mousemove with no rAF coalescing, re-allocating the canvas backing store and forcing layout each time
findings.claim: Aeon's level viewport subscribes to vpX/vpY/zoom as zustand selectors and does a full recompose in a dep-driven effect, so a pan drag issues one complete redraw per mousemove (hundreds/sec on a high-poll mouse) — each of which calls getBoundingClientRect and reassigns canvas.width/height — the exact pattern its classic sibling documents as the redraw storm it removed.
findings.evidence: MapViewport.tsx:122-124 subscribes `vpX`, `vpY`, `zoom` via selectors; handleMouseMove calls `pan(dx, dy)` on every mousemove while dragging (MapViewport.tsx:1257-1262), and object drags call `bumpLiveEdit()` per move (:1252) — `liveEditVersion` is also in the deps. The redraw effect at :430-476 lists vpX, vpY, zoom, liveEditVersion in its dep array, so it runs once per store tick with NO requestAnimationFrame anywhere in the file (`grep -n requestAnimationFrame MapViewport.tsx` → no hits). Inside it: `container.getBoundingClientRect()` (:438) forces a synchronous layout, then `canvas.width = rect.width; canvas.height = rect.height` (:439-440) — the standard clear-the-canvas idiom, i.e. it reinitializes the bitmap even when the size is unchanged: ~4.5 MB alloc+zero for a 1400x800 canvas, per mousemove. Then a full-canvas fillRect + N section drawImages + overlayRenderer.render (:462-472), and overlayRenderer's collision path is A1's per-column stroke loop (OverlayRenderer.ts:214-223). ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:160-199 does the opposite deliberately, and says so: 'Written ONLY by the measure/ResizeObserver path ... the render pass reads it and never resizes the canvas (assigning width/height reinitializes the backing store) nor forces layout via getBoundingClientRect, so drags stay cheap', with rAF coalescing at :181-199 and a guard test at classic-camera.test.ts:9-13. MapViewport has neither half. At 500 events/s that is ~2.2 GB/s of backing-store alloc+memset, 500 forced layouts/s, and ~490 of every 500 recomposites discarded before paint.
findings.fix: Port ClassicLevelViewport's shape: hold the camera in a ref, publish to viewStore once per painted frame from inside a single rAF, adopt external writes with an imperative `useViewStore.subscribe`, and move the canvas.width/height assignment into the existing ResizeObserver path (:479-520) so the render pass never resizes or measures.

verdict.reasoning:
I traced the whole path and could not break it. Trigger: open an aeon level tab with an act loaded, pick the `view` tool (or hold middle mouse) and drag. `handleMouseMove` (MapViewport.tsx:1155) falls through to the pan branch and calls `pan(dx, dy)` at :1259 on every dispatched mousemove; `isDragging.current` is armed at :885 (tool==='view' || e.button===1) and at :942 (select-tool click on empty space). viewStore.ts:77-80 `pan` sets new vpX/vpY unconditionally — no equality guard, no throttle. The redraw effect's dep array (MapViewport.tsx:476) contains vpX, vpY, zoom, liveEditVersion, so it re-runs per store tick, and there is no requestAnimationFrame anywhere in the file (grep confirms zero hits). Inside the effect: container.getBoundingClientRect() at :438, then UNGUARDED `canvas.width = rect.width; canvas.height = rect.height` at :439-440 (no `if (canvas.width !== w)`), then the full fillRect + culled drawImages + overlayRenderer.render. No guard the seat missed.

The classic contrast is quoted accurately: ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:159-163 holds the sizeRef comment verbatim, :182-199 is the rAF coalescer, :204-215 the imperative useViewStore.subscribe adopt path, and classic/__tests__/classic-camera.test.ts guards all three. The only thing resembling a defense of MapViewport is that test file's header comment ("a performance bug HERE and not there"), whose stated reason is that classic's render effect has no dep array — that reason does not apply, because MapViewport's dep array *contains the camera fields*, so its effect re-runs on exactly the same ticks. The comment is wrong, not a mitigation.

Two corrections to the seat's evidence. (1) UNDERSTATED: the ResizeObserver effect at :479-520 also lists vpX, vpY, zoom, liveEditVersion in its deps (:520), so every pan mousemove disconnects and re-constructs the observer; a newly observed element always receives an initial notification, and that callback (:484-518) does its own canvas.width/height assignment plus a second complete renderBg/render/overlayRenderer.render. A drag frame therefore costs roughly TWO full composites plus observer churn, which the seat never mentions. (2) OVERSTATED: the arithmetic (500 events/s, ~2.2 GB/s, 500 forced layouts/s, ~490 of 500 composites discarded pre-paint) does not hold in Electron — Chromium coalesces mousemove in the main-thread event queue and dispatches at most one per BeginFrame, so a high-poll mouse produces ~refresh-rate listener calls, not hundreds-to-thousands, and essentially nothing is discarded before paint. The composite is also cheaper than implied: SectionRenderer.render (SectionRenderer.ts:386-412) frustum-culls and drawImages cached 2048px section canvases — a few blits, not a tile recompose.

The proposed fix is the right shape, but it must also strip vpX/vpY/zoom from the ResizeObserver effect's deps, otherwise the per-frame churn is merely relocated.
verdict.severity_correction: Downgrade high -> medium. Nothing here produces wrong output or loses user work: pans, object drags and the composite all render correctly, and the redundant backing-store reset is invisible because the pass repaints the full canvas anyway. What is real is redundant per-frame work on a main-path gesture (~2 full composites instead of 1, plus one forced layout, one backing-store reinit and one ResizeObserver rebuild per frame). Real cleanup with a known-good sibling implementation to copy, but a perf/quality finding, not "wrong output or broken main-path feature" — and the seat's headline numbers, which are what make it read as high, are inflated by roughly an order of magnitude by Chromium's per-frame mousemove coalescing.

findings.title: BlockTab/ChunkTab thumbnail strips still key on the coarse chunkEpoch — one block-cell click repaints all ~1400 thumbnails
findings.claim: The per-entity thumbnail invalidation that TileTab was fixed to use never landed on BlockTab or ChunkTab: both pass `String(chunkEpoch)` as the versionKey for their whole strips, so a single block edit repaints all 439 BlockThumbs AND all ~965 TileThumbs — including the tile strip, which by the store's own reasoning a block edit cannot invalidate.
findings.evidence: BlockTab.tsx:337 `const versionKey = String(chunkEpoch);` is passed to every BlockThumb (:455) and every TileThumb (:469); ChunkTab.tsx:431/:543 does the same for its 439 BlockThumbs. TileThumb/BlockThumb repaint whenever versionKey changes (composer-thumbs.tsx:59-64 and :89-93 have versionKey in their effect deps). A block edit commits `commitArt(newDoc, { blocks: true }, { kind: 'all' })` (classicLevelStore.ts:843), and applyCommit bumps chunkEpoch for kind:'all' (classicLevelStore.ts:653-655) — so every BlockTab click invalidates both strips. TileTab was explicitly fixed for this and says so at TileTab.tsx:386-391: 'Keying the whole strip on chunkEpoch repainted all 965 thumbnails on every committed pencil stroke; this repaints the one tile the stroke actually wrote', using `versionKeyFor(id) = `${paletteEpoch}:${tileVersions.get(id) ?? 0}``. Worse, applyCommit's own comment at classicLevelStore.ts:663-665 states 'a block edit bumps NEITHER [paletteEpoch nor tileEpoch]: no object sprite and no tile thumbnail bakes block data, so a block edit must invalidate none of them' — BlockTab defeats that by feeding chunkEpoch to TileThumb anyway. Cost per click: 439 renderBlock + 965 renderTile, each ending in drawBufferScaled, which creates a throwaway <canvas> element per call (see A5) → ~1404 canvas element creations, contexts, ImageData allocations and scaled blits per click.
findings.fix: BlockTab's tile strip can be fixed today: use TileTab's `versionKeyFor(id)` (`${paletteEpoch}:${tileVersions.get(id) ?? 0}`) for the TileThumbs at BlockTab.tsx:469 — the store already publishes both clocks. For the block strips, add a `blockVersions: Map<number, number>` clock alongside `chunkVersions` in classicLevelStore (bumped from the same `nextVersion()` allocator by classicEditBlock / the surface plan's blockWrites) and key BlockThumb on `${paletteEpoch}:${blockVersions.get(id) ?? 0}:${tileEpoch}`.

verdict.reasoning:
Traced end to end and could not break the path. (1) BlockTab.tsx:337 `const versionKey = String(chunkEpoch);` (chunkEpoch subscribed at :84) is passed to every BlockThumb (:455, over `doc.blocks.map` — 439 on GHZ) and every TileThumb (:469, over `Array.from({length: tileCount})` where `tileCount = doc.tiles.length/32` = 965); neither strip is virtualized. (2) composer-thumbs.tsx:59-64 (TileThumb) and :89-93 (BlockThumb) both have `versionKey` in the draw-effect deps and are memoized on primitives, so a changed versionKey re-renders AND re-runs drawScaled -> drawBufferScaled, which creates a throwaway <canvas> + context + ImageData per call (composer-shared.tsx:230-237). (3) The commit side matches: BlockTab's editCell (:276-289) calls classicEditBlock -> commitArt(newDoc, {blocks:true}, {kind:'all'}) (classicLevelStore.ts:843) -> applyCommit :653-655 sets chunkEpoch = nextVersion() for kind:'all', while :667-676 deliberately leaves paletteEpoch/tileEpoch/tileVersions untouched for a block edit ("a block edit must invalidate none of them"). So BlockTab defeats the store's own reasoning by feeding chunkEpoch to 965 TileThumbs. (4) TileTab genuinely was fixed and BlockTab/ChunkTab were not: TileTab.tsx:391 uses `${paletteEpoch}:${tileVersions.get(id) ?? 0}` at :510, while grep shows BlockTab :337/:455/:469 and ChunkTab :431/:543 still on String(chunkEpoch). Concrete trigger: GHZ act 1, Block tab Assign mode, click any tile in the Tiles strip (or a flip/priority/palette chip) -> classicEditBlock -> chunkEpoch bump -> 439 renderBlock + 965 renderTile, each with a fresh canvas + scaled blit; likewise on every committed stroke in Block-tab Paint mode (classicPaintSurface also commits {kind:'all'}).

Three corrections that do not refute it: (a) the title's literal trigger is wrong — onCellClick (:305-313) only sets selection and commits nothing (it does change cell.pal, which re-keys the tile strip through the separate `palLine` prop, independent of this bug); the committing triggers are the assign/flip/palette edits and paint strokes. (b) The block-strip half is NOT a straight port of TileTab's fix: chunkEpoch is currently the only published signal that a block changed, so BlockThumb's coarse key is load-bearing for correctness until the proposed `blockVersions` clock exists — only the tile strip at :469 is fixable today, exactly as the fix note says. (c) ChunkTab's exposure is smaller than implied: chunk-cell edits commit {kind:'chunk', id} (classicLevelStore.ts:823), which bumps chunkVersions and not chunkEpoch, so ChunkTab's 439 BlockThumbs do not repaint while painting chunk cells — only on block/tile/palette commits and its own paint-mode strokes.
verdict.severity_correction: medium — output is always correct (the coarse clock over-invalidates, never under-invalidates); nothing is lost, corrupted, or misdrawn, and no feature is broken. The 9-second freeze cited in composer-thumbs.tsx:14-32 came from React DEV deep-diffing the `doc` OBJECT prop, which no longer applies here since every thumb prop is a primitive. What is left is ~1404 redundant small rasterizes (8x8 / 16x16) plus temp-canvas blits per commit — a per-stroke hitch in Block-tab paint/assign, i.e. a real efficiency defect but not "wrong output or broken main-path feature".

findings.title: drawBufferScaled creates and discards a whole <canvas> element on every thumbnail paint
findings.claim: Every composer thumbnail repaint allocates a fresh DOM canvas element plus a 2D context as its upscale source, so opening the Tile tab creates ~965 throwaway canvases and one BlockTab click creates ~1400 — even though the codebase already uses a shared scratch canvas for exactly this job elsewhere.
findings.evidence: composer-shared.tsx:230-237: `const tmp = document.createElement('canvas'); tmp.width = srcW; tmp.height = srcH; const tctx = tmp.getContext('2d', { willReadFrequently: true }); ... ctx.drawImage(tmp, ...)`. srcW/srcH are only 8x8 or 16x16, so the element itself — not the pixels — is the cost: a DOM node, a CanvasRenderingContext2D, and a Skia surface per call. Callers: composer-thumbs.tsx:39-41 (`drawScaled` → drawBufferScaled) from both TileThumb (:63) and BlockThumb (:92). TileTab.tsx:508-515 renders `tileCount` (≈965 on GHZ) TileThumbs, each of which paints on mount → ~965 element creations on tab open; combined with A4, one BlockTab click is ~1404. The shared-scratch pattern already exists in this repo for the same problem — ChunkGrid.tsx:130-139 builds one module-level scratch canvas with `willReadFrequently` and reuses it, and ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:297-307 explains the same lesson.
findings.fix: Hoist a module-level scratch canvas in composer-shared.tsx keyed on (srcW, srcH) — resize it only when the source dimensions change — exactly as ChunkGrid.tsx:130-139 does, and drawImage from it.

findings.title: PixelViewport recomposes the entire buffer to RGBA on every render, including every pointermove of a stroke
findings.claim: The draw effect has no dependency array and allocates a fresh OffscreenCanvas + ImageData and walks every pixel each time it runs, and `rerender()` fires it on every pointermove — so dragging in ChunkTab paint mode does a 65,536-iteration recompose plus a 256 KB ImageData allocation per mouse event, on top of a full-canvas upscale blit.
findings.evidence: PixelViewport.tsx:112 `useEffect(() => {...})` closes at :200 with `});` — no dep array, so it runs after every render. Inside: `const off = new OffscreenCanvas(width, height)` (:123), `octx.createImageData(width, height)` (:125), a `for (let i = 0; i < width * height; i++)` palette-resolve loop (:126-139), putImageData (:140), clearRect over the full destination (:144) and drawImage upscaled to `width*zoom` (:155). onPointerMove calls `controller.move(...)` then `rerender()` (:238-239), and rerender is `force(n => n + 1)` (:100-101). Buffer sizes at each host: TileTab 8x8 = 64 iterations (harmless); SpriteCanvasHost typically 32x32; aeon ComposerCanvas 128x128 = 16,384 iterations + 64 KB ImageData per move; ChunkTab paint 256x256 (classic-surface-buffer.ts:110/:66) = 65,536 iterations + 256 KB ImageData per move, and the drawImage at :155 upscales into a `256*zoom` square — 6144x6144 = 37.7 M destination pixels at the previous default zoom 24. Nothing between the buffer and the RGBA offscreen is memoised, even though only the overlay layer (selection/preview, :178-197) changes between moves within a gesture.
findings.fix: Split the effect: memoise the buffer→OffscreenCanvas composition on `[shown, palette, paletteLines, lineMap, layers.checkerboard/checkerScale/checkerColors, width, height]` (a useMemo/useRef keeping one reusable OffscreenCanvas sized to the buffer), and keep only the blit + grids + selection + preview in the dep-less pass. That makes a pointermove cost one drawImage plus vector overlays instead of a full palette resolve and two allocations.

findings.title: findPoolMatch re-canonicalises the whole 965-tile pool for every wanted tile — O(unique x pool) with two allocations per inner step
findings.claim: The flip-aware pool match rebuilds every pool tile's canonical form from scratch on each call, and the canvas commit calls it once per unique resolved tile, so a commit is quadratic in (unique tiles x pool size) and allocates a 64-byte array plus a 64-character string per inner iteration.
findings.evidence: tile-pool-match.ts:126-139: `for (let t = 0; t < count; t++) { ... const canon = canonicalTile(poolTileEntries(pool, t, scratch)); ... }` — `count = floor(pool.length / 32)` (:114), ~965 for a GHZ act. canonicalTile (tile-canon.ts:75-99) allocates `new Uint8Array(TILE_ENTRIES)` (:92) and `String.fromCharCode(...scratch)` (:96) on every call, after a tie-breaking scan that is up to 64x4 index computations (:82-90). Caller: classic-commit-plan.ts:307-310 loops `for (const t of res.tiles)` and calls `findPoolMatch(doc.tiles, want, avail, { allowFlips: true })` inside. `res.tiles` is the deduped unique-tile list from resolveCanvasRegion (canvas-resolve.ts:108-121), but tile-canon.ts:48 documents 'a max-size canvas holds 16 384 of them'. For a modest 500-unique-tile commit against a 965-tile pool that is 482,500 canonicalTile calls → ~482k Uint8Array(64) + ~482k 64-char strings ≈ 100 MB of garbage and a multi-hundred-ms to multi-second synchronous freeze on the commit click. Supporting waste on the same path: `unavailableForAllocation(avail)` (tile-pool-match.ts:46-48) builds a brand-new Set from both sets, and `freeSlot()` calls it on every allocation (classic-commit-plan.ts:291), making allocation O(k^2) in the number of claimed slots; findFreeSlot in classic-surface-plan.ts:277 does the same per edited cell. The non-flip path (classic-surface-plan.ts:266) is cheaper but still 965x32 byte compares per edited tile — a chunk-surface stroke touching many cells multiplies that.
findings.fix: Build the pool's canonical index once per plan: a `Map<key, tileIndex>` over the 965 pool tiles, constructed before the `res.tiles` loop and passed into findPoolMatch (with `allocated` filtered at lookup time). That turns the commit from O(unique x pool) into O(pool + unique). Separately, keep a single mutable `taken` Set in classic-commit-plan's freeSlot instead of rebuilding it via unavailableForAllocation per call.

findings.title: The sprite editor is the one PixelViewport host that does not apply cappedZoom
findings.claim: SpriteCanvasHost hands PixelViewport the raw store zoom, so a large sprite frame at high zoom can produce a canvas past the platform edge limit — which renders blank with no error, the exact failure zoom-cap.ts was written to prevent — and an unbounded backing store on the way there.
findings.evidence: SpriteCanvasHost.tsx:69-73 renders `<PixelViewport ... zoom={zoom} />` with `zoom` taken straight from `useSpriteStore((s) => s.zoom)` (:32); the file imports no cappedZoom (`grep -n cappedZoom SpriteCanvasHost.tsx` → nothing). Every other host applies it: TileTab.tsx:186, ChunkTab.tsx:195, BlockTab.tsx:165, ComposerCanvas.tsx:157. zoom-cap.ts:11-14 states the rule was extracted 'so classic's tile host can apply the identical rule rather than open-code a second one', and zoom-cap.ts:1-8 states the consequence of exceeding it: 'a <canvas> past the platform's maximum dimension does not clip or fail loudly — it comes back BLANK, and every host that renders one goes white with no error'. spriteStore.ts:456 clamps zoom to 1..48; PixelViewport.tsx:254 sizes the canvas at `width * zoom`. A 128x128 loaded frame at zoom 48 is 6144^2*4 = 151 MB (the same figure artStore.ts:78 calls a defect); a 384-px-wide frame at 48 crosses 16000 px and goes blank. The default 32x32 frame (spriteStore.ts:192) is safe, so this only bites on imported/large frames — but nothing bounds frame size at the host.
findings.fix: `const effectiveZoom = cappedZoom(zoom, Math.max(buffer.width, buffer.height))` in SpriteCanvasHost and pass that to PixelViewport (the hit-test uses the same value, so this is a one-line change), plus the area bound from A2 once it exists.

findings.title: chunkEpoch is bumped by every tile, block and palette edit, wiping the whole level-viewport chunk-canvas cache
findings.claim: Any art edit that is not a single-chunk edit bumps the coarse chunkEpoch, which is part of the classic viewport's cache key, so one composer pencil stroke forces every visible chunk canvas to be re-composed from scratch even though the reverse indices needed to narrow it already exist.
findings.evidence: applyCommit sets `chunkEpoch = nextVersion()` for `ve.kind === 'all'` (classicLevelStore.ts:653-655), and every tile edit (:875), block edit (:843), surface paint (:989, :1103) and palette edit (:1127) passes kind:'all'. ClassicLevelViewport keys its per-chunk cache on `${chunkEpoch}:${chunkVersions.get(chunkId) ?? 0}` (ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:472), and getChunkCanvas re-renders on any key mismatch (:292-316). Cost per invalidated chunk: renderChunk allocates a fresh `Uint8ClampedArray(256*256*4)` = 256 KB (render.ts:126), composes 65,536 pixels through up to 256 blitRgba calls with a per-call block cache (:137-153), then getChunkCanvas allocates another 256 KB ImageData and does a putImageData (ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:312-314). At the ~45 chunks visible at GHZ1's fit zoom (48x5 grid from /home/volence/sonic_hacks/s1disasm/levels/ghz1.bin) that is ~23 MB of allocation and ~2.9 M pixel composes per committed stroke while the composer dock is open over the map. The narrowing data exists: buildUsageIndex publishes tileToBlocks and blockToChunks (usage-index.ts:37-42), so a tile edit knows exactly which chunk ids it can reach.
findings.fix: Replace the blanket chunkEpoch bump for tile/block edits with a targeted `chunkVersions` bump over `blockToChunks` of the affected blocks (for a block edit) or `tileToBlocks` → `blockToChunks` (for a tile edit), reserving chunkEpoch for genuinely global changes (palette, act reload). Keep chunkEpoch as the fallback when the usage index is unavailable.

findings.title: objectIdSig walks every object and builds a sorted joined string on every render, including every rAF redraw
findings.claim: The object-sprite refresh signature is computed inline in the component body rather than memoised, so it re-walks the act's object list, allocates a key string per object, builds a Set, sorts and joins on every render — and this component re-renders once per painted frame throughout a pan or object drag.
findings.evidence: ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:347-349: `const objectIdSig = doc && ref ? [...new Set(doc.objects.map((o) => objectArtKey(o.id, ref.zone, o.subtype)))].sort().join(',') : '';` sits in the component body with no useMemo. The component re-renders on every rAF via `forceRedraw((n) => n + 1)` (:197), which the redraw() path schedules on every mousemove of a pan/stamp/object drag (:181-199). objectArtKey builds a template string per object. GHZ1's objpos file is 402 bytes = ~66 placements, but denser acts run into the low hundreds; each frame therefore allocates one string per object plus a Set, a spread array, a sort and a join. Small in absolute terms (tens of microseconds per frame) but it is unnecessary garbage on the one path the rest of this component was carefully engineered to keep allocation-free.
findings.fix: `const objectIdSig = useMemo(() => ..., [doc, ref])` — doc identity already changes on every commit, which is exactly when the signature can change.
